land.text: the Kabul-Arachosia country (51), Mathura and Sialkot (91): Cliopatria draws these in the Indo-Scythian shape

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessors: Indo-Greek Kingdom, Indo-Parthian Kingdom, Indo-Scythians, Northern Satraps, Western Satraps, Maha-meghavahanas. The Kushans were born on nobody's land in Bactria (the Yuezhi confederation) and absorbed these states afterwards, from c. 51.

land.text: Gandhara, Taxila, the Punjab and Sindh, 'displaced' by Kujula Kadphises and his son, absorbed in 91 in Cliopatria

predecessors.note: Kujula Kadphises page: he and his son 'seem to have displaced the Indo-Parthian kingdom' after 45 CE.

land.text: Fergana (Dayuan): the last Great Yuan shape, 168 of whose 172 cells lie inside the Kushan shape of 51

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's reading only: the Kushan Empire page (re-read 2026-10-19) does not mention Fergana, Ferghana or Dayuan. The great-yuan dossier (ia-01) lists kushan-empire among its successors; its 50 dissolve should name kushan-empire as counterpart.

land.text: the Punjab, Gandhara, Taxila and the Gangetic plain: based in the Punjab with its capital at Taxila (Kushan Empire page)

capitals.name: Kapisa (Begram)
capitals.note: Kushan Empire infobox (re-read 2026-10-19): 'Capital: 1st Century BCE: Kapisa/Pushkalavati; from 1st century CE: Purushapura/Mathura; 3rd and 4th centuries CE: Taxila'. Kapisa lies inside the 43 and 51 shapes; Pushkalavati and Purushapura (Gandhara) lie outside the 43 shape and Peshawar enters only with the Gandhara added to the 51 shape. The infobox dates by century; the move from Kapisa is placed at 91, when Mathura enters the shape (reviewer, sa-02-c: the capital dot must lie inside the drawn shape).

capitals.name: Purushapura (Peshawar)
capitals.note: Kanishka page: 'The main capital of his empire was located at Puruṣapura'. Kushan Empire infobox: 'from 1st century CE: Purushapura/Mathura'. Reviewer (sa-02-c) moved the start from 30 to 91 because Peshawar lies outside Cliopatria's 43 shape and is inside the corrected 51 shape only from 51; 91 is a bridging choice (confidence 1).

capitals.name: Mathura
capitals.note: Second major capital and winter seat (Kanishka page: Mathura is the second major capital); Kapisa was the summer capital under Kanishka (Kushan Empire page). Mathura joins the Kushan shape in 91 (Northern Satraps page: Mathura 'became part of the Kushan Empire from the reign of Vima Kadphises (90-100 CE)').

rulers.name: Kujula Kadphises
rulers.note: Infobox 25-85 (Kujula Kadphises page: approximately 25 to 85 CE); the Kushan Empire body text places the reign about 50-90, Bopearachchi 40-90 (and 30-80 on the Kujula page). Heraios (c. 1-30) is the first to call himself Kushan on coins and 'may have been' the same person. Reviewer (sa-02-c): clipped to the state's life (from 30, the confederation) and ended at c. 90 per the Kushan Empire page's list ('Kujula Kadphises (c. 50 - c. 90)') so that it meets Vima Takto (c. 90).

rulers.name: Vima Kadphises
rulers.note: Vima Kadphises page infobox: 'Reign: 113-127 CE'; the Kushan Empire page also gives c. 95-127 and its succession box 90-100.

rulers.name: Kanishka the Great
rulers.note: Accession 127 (Falk, Kanishka page); 'c. 151' end (Kushan Empire page), 150/151 on the Kanishka page.

rulers.name: Vasudeva I
rulers.note: The Kushan Empire list gives c. 190-230; its body text says he died in 225, the year the empire split.

correction.text: the 43 shape unchanged, held from c. 30: the Yuezhi confederation in Bactria

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria begins in 43; the Kushan Empire page's infobox gives Established c. 30 CE, when Kujula Kadphises unified the Yuezhi tribes into a confederation, and the Kujula Kadphises page 'united the Yuezhi confederation in Bactria'. The 43 shape (Bactria, Sogdia and the Tajik-Uzbek foothills) is held back 13 years. No page opened gives an area for this period.

0.46 M km2 for 43-50: Bactria (44% of the shape), Sogdia, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. The Kujula Kadphises page says he 'united the Yuezhi confederation in Bactria during the 1st century CE'; no infobox area exists for this period, so only the place is checked.

Cliopatria's shape is 0.64 M km2 for 51-90 (Kabul country, Arachosia, Fergana, Sogdia added) and holds Kabul but only 64 of the 193 cells of Gandhara and none of Taxila or Peshawar, because Cliopatria keeps them in the Indo-Parthian shape until 90. The Hou Hanshu passage on the Kushan Empire page has Kujula take the Gaofu (Kabul) region and 'defeat the whole of the kingdoms of Puda (Paktiya) and Jibin (Kapisha and Gandhara)'; the Indo-Parthian Kingdom page (re-read 2026-10-19) has the Kushans under Kujula Kadphises 'begin absorbing the northern Indian part of the kingdom' from the middle of the 1st century; indo-parthians /ledger/2 loses Gandhara, Taxila and Kabulistan to the Kushans in 50 and its keyframes 51 and 84 already exclude them. Reviewer (sa-02-c): verdict changed from ok to adjust, adding the 133 cells (about 34,000 km2) so that the land is not left stateless in 51-90; the 91 gain from indo-parthians is reduced to the Punjab and Sindh remainder (1,683 cells, the same cells as indo-parthians /ledger/3). The 231 cells in Arachosia (Kandahar) are not on any page opened.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 51 shape plus Gandhara and Taxila: the 133 cells of the Indo-Parthian shape of 84 inside Gandhara, a 100 km circle round Taxila and Kabulistan, which the Hou Hanshu's Jibin (Kapisha and Gandhara) puts under Kujula Kadphises; Peshawar (Purushapura) is in the corrected shape

Mathura is placed here by Cliopatria although the Vima Kadphises page, which only says he 'may have replaced the Indo-Scythian ruler Sodasa in Mathura', dates him 113-127. The Kanishka page's footnote (quoting Dutt) names Punjab, Sind, Gujarat, Agra and Rajputana as part of Kanishka's empire; the Rudradaman page lists Sindhu-Sauvira, Maru and Kukura among Rudradaman's lands in 150 (see notes).

The pages opened name only Kashgar (the Kushans installed Chenpan as king of Kashgar in the Yuanchu period, 114-120) and 'forays into the Tarim Basin' under Kanishka; the Kanishka page calls Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand Chinese dependencies. Reviewer (sa-02-c): the earlier correction subtracted the Tarim Basin region, which left 156 cells (about 39,000 km2) of the rim in the direct shape through 183 with no event; the correction now subtracts the strip itself (the 117 shape minus the 91 shape). Kashgar is a client king, not direct land, so it is left out of this shape and drawn only by the ledger's vassal_start/vassal_end (117-127), not twice.

1.94 M km2 against the infobox 2.0-2.5 M km2 (c. 200): ratio 0.78-0.97, in range. The corrected 117-183 shapes already exclude the Tarim strip, so the corrected 165 shape and Cliopatria's 184 shape differ by only 4 cells; Cliopatria's 165-to-184 drop of 892 strip cells needs no event in the direct shape. 1.94 M km2, 19 cells different from 184; no page dates any change in 215.

correction.text: unchanged shape, held 224-225 only; from 226 the same land is the union of the Eastern Kushans' and Western Kushans' shapes

keyframe_review.note: The shape is Cliopatria's 224-237 outline (1.94 M km2) but the Kushan Empire page says 'After the death of Vasudeva I in 225, the Kushan empire split into western and eastern halves', so it holds only 224-225 here. 226-237 belong to the two successor dossiers: the Eastern Kushans' 238 shape and the Western Kushans' 238 shape together make up 99% of this one.

region.text: the Yuezhi confederation in Bactria (Cliopatria's first Kushan shape)

ledger.note: c. 30: Kujula Kadphises unifies the Yuezhi tribes into the Kushan confederation in Bactria. The infobox gives Established c. 30 CE, when Kujula Kadphises unified the Yuezhi tribes into a confederation; the Kujula Kadphises page says he 'united the Yuezhi confederation in Bactria'. The page gives 'c.', and its own reign figures for Kujula differ (25-85 infobox, about 50-90 body).

region.text: Kabul and Arachosia: the part of the 51 growth that lies inside Cliopatria's Indo-Scythian shape

ledger.note: c. 51: Kujula Kadphises takes the Kabul country. Hou Hanshu on the page: he 'invaded Anxi (Indo-Parthia), and took the Gaofu ([Kabul]) region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms of Puda ([Paktiya]) and Jibin ([Kapisha] and [Gandhara])'. The page gives no year; the Kujula Kadphises page dates the Indo-Parthian invasion 'some time after 45 CE'. 51 is Cliopatria's year, and Cliopatria draws this land (Kabul, Arachosia) in the Indo-Scythian shape, not the Indo-Parthian one the page names.

region.text: Fergana (Dayuan): the 168 cells of the 51 growth that lie inside Cliopatria's last Great Yuan shape

ledger.note: c. 51: the Fergana basin enters the Kushan shape. Cliopatria's Great Yuan row ends in 50 (168 of its 172 cells of 43 lie in the Kushan shape of 51) and great-yuan lists kushan-empire as successor. The Kushan Empire page (re-read 2026-10-19) does not mention Fergana, Ferghana or Dayuan; it names Sogdiana only as a land where traces of the Kushans remain and which the Sasanians later took. Year and taker are Cliopatria's reading (confidence 1). Reviewer (sa-02-c): this land was 'nobody' before; great-yuan's 50 dissolve should name kushan-empire as counterpart (ia-01).

region.text: Gandhara and Taxila: the 133 cells of the Indo-Parthian shape of 84 that the corrected 51 shape adds (the Hou Hanshu's Jibin)

ledger.note: c. 51: Kujula Kadphises takes Gandhara and Taxila. Hou Hanshu on the Kushan Empire page: he 'invaded Anxi (Indo-Parthia), and took the Gaofu ([Kabul]) region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms of Puda ([Paktiya]) and Jibin ([Kapisha] and [Gandhara])'. The Indo-Parthian Kingdom page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'from the middle of the 1st century AD the Kushans under Kujula Kadphises began absorbing the northern Indian part of the kingdom'; it gives no year for Gandhara or Taxila. 51 is Cliopatria's year for the Kushan shape; indo-parthians /ledger/2 has the loss in 50 and its keyframes 51 and 84 already exclude these cells (one year apart). Cliopatria draws them Indo-Parthian until 90; the keyframe 51 verdict is adjust for this reason (reviewer, sa-02-c).

region.text: the 13 cells of the 51 growth (Fergana edge, Gandhara edge) held by no Cliopatria state

ledger.note: c. 51: a few edge cells of the north-eastern Bactrian growth join the Kushan shape; no page opened mentions them, so the year and the land are Cliopatria's. (11 of the 13 lie in Cliopatria's Indo-Parthian shape of 43, which differs from its shape of 84 by a few cells.)

c. 90: the seat moves from Kapisa to Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura. Kushan Empire infobox: 'Capital: 1st Century BCE: Kapisa/Pushkalavati; from 1st century CE: Purushapura/Mathura'; the Kanishka page (reign from 127, Falk) has 'The main capital of his empire was located at Puruṣapura' and Mathura as the second major capital. The infobox dates by century only; 91 is when Mathura joins the shape. Reviewer (sa-02-c): moved here from 127 so that the capital dot lies inside the drawn shape.

region.text: the Indo-Parthian remainder: Punjab and Sindh (Gandhara and Taxila came in 51)

ledger.note: c. 90: Vima Takto carries the Kushans over the rest of the Indo-Parthian land in north-west India. 'He expanded the Kushan Empire into the northwest of South Asia'; the Hou Hanshu says he 'defeated Tianzhu [North-western India] and installed Generals to supervise and lead it'. The page names no cities; the land is the Indo-Parthian shape of 84-90 minus Gandhara, Taxila and the Kabul valley (Multan, Sindh, the Punjab), 1,683 cells, the same cells as indo-parthians /ledger/3 (90). Gandhara and Taxila entered the shape in 51 (reviewer, sa-02-c).

region.text: Mathura, Sialkot and the eastern Punjab, from the Indo-Scythian shape

ledger.note: c. 90: Mathura and Sialkot enter the Kushan shape. Northern Satraps page (read 2026-10-19): 'Mathura became part of the Kushan Empire from the reign of Vima Kadphises (90-100 CE)' and the Northern Satraps were 'probably displaced by, or became vassals of, the Kushans from the time of Vima Kadphises'. The Vima Kadphises page, by contrast, dates his reign 113-127 and says only that he 'may have replaced the Indo-Scythian ruler Sodasa in Mathura'. The Indo-Scythian shape shrinks from 1,710 to 449 cells in 91; the region (Mathura, Sialkot, the eastern Punjab) is the reading of the shape.

region.text: the Punjab, Haryana and Kashmir cells of the 91 growth outside both neighbours' shapes

ledger.note: c. 90: the Haryana, upper Punjab and Kashmir cells that no Cliopatria state held join the Kushan shape with the rest of the 'northwest of South Asia'.

region.text: Kashgar, where the Kushans installed Chenpan as king

ledger.note: 114-120: the Kushans put their own king on the throne of Kashgar. In the Yuanchu period (AD 114-120) the Kushans installed Chenpan as king of Kashgar (Kushan Empire page). Rounded to Cliopatria's 117. The page does not say whether Kashgar paid tribute; a client king is drawn as a vassal tint. Reviewer (sa-02-c): the circle is drawn only by this event; the keyframes 117-165 leave Kashgar out of the direct shape.

c. 127: the Kashgar client kingdom ends. The Shule Kingdom page (read 2026-10-19) lists 'Chen Pan (臣磐) 127' among its kings and says 'In 127 AD, Shule began to pay tribute to the Eastern Han'; it does not mention the Kushans, so the end of the Kushan relation is inferred from the change of tribute, not stated. The Kushan Empire page has only the installation of Chenpan in 114-120 and the Kanishka page calls Kashgar, Khotan and Yarkand Chinese dependencies. The earlier year 184 was Cliopatria's year for the 889 strip cells it gives to the Protectorate of the Western Regions; with the strip removed from the direct shapes (keyframes 117-165) nothing in the Kushan shape changes in 184. Reviewer (sa-02-c): moved from 184 on the Shule page.

region.text: Awadh, the Doab, western Bihar and the Vindhyan tip: the cities of the Rabatak inscription (Saketa, Kausambi, Pataliputra, Champa)

ledger.note: 127: Kanishka's first year (the Rabatak inscription) and the Gangetic plain. The inscription says he 'had submitted all India to (his) will' and lists Ujjain, Kundina, Saketa, Kausambi, Pataliputra and Champa; 'Kushan territory in India extended at least as far as Saketa and Sarnath near Varanasi', and a Chinese text of 472 'refers to the conquest of Pataliputra by Kanishka' (undated). No Cliopatria state held the Gangetic cells, so 'nobody'; the page names no local kings.

region.text: the Western Satraps' realm (Ujjain, Malwa, Gujarat, Saurashtra), held by Chastana's line

ledger.note: 127: the Western Satraps are drawn as Kushan vassals (the 'early period'). Western Satraps page (re-read 2026-10-19): 'the position taken by modern scholarship is that the Western Satraps were vassals of the Kushans, at least in the early period until Rudradaman I conquered the Yaudheyas, who are usually thought to be Kushan vassals. The question is not considered perfectly settled'; the lead says it is 'still unclear whether the Western Satraps were independent rulers or vassals'; the Rabatak inscription 'claims Kushan dominion over Western Satrap territory' under Kanishka (c. 127-150) and the Chastana statue at Mathura 'suggests Castana may have been a feudatory'. The Chastana page gives no date for any relation. No page dates the start: 127 is Kanishka's year 1, the first Kushan claim to Ujjain (Kanishka page lists Ujjain among the Rabatak cities). Mirrored by western-satraps /ledger (vassal_start 127, vassal_end 150, counterpart kushan-empire).

150: the Kushan suzerainty over the Western Satraps ends. The Western Satraps page ties the end of the 'early period' to Rudradaman I's conquest of the Yaudheyas (undated); Rudradaman reigned 130-150 (Rudradaman page) and the Junagadh inscription, the record of his conquests, is dated 150. 150 is the last year of the reign and a bridging choice; the reviewer (sa-02-c) suggested c. 130, Rudradaman's accession, which would leave only three years of vassalage (127-129). Replaces the earlier end in 225. Mirrored by western-satraps /ledger.

region.text: Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand and the edges of Bihar and Madhya Pradesh

ledger.note: c. 161: the south-eastern tip of the Gangetic gains (Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, around 'Champa') leaves the Kushan shape. Page-silent: the Kushan Empire page says only that the Rabatak text 'is not clear whether Champa was a possession of Kanishka or just beyond it'. The Huvishka page (read 2026-10-19) describes no loss or retreat of Kushan territory.

region.text: Bactria, Sogdia and the Kabul valley

ledger.note: 225: the western half of the empire is divided from the Punjab and the Gangetic plain. 'After the death of Vasudeva I in 225, the Kushan empire split into western and eastern halves.' The Western half was 'soon subjugated by the Persian Sasanian Empire' (same page). The Vasudeva I dates differ on the page (died 225; list c. 190-230). Cliopatria starts the two halves in 238.

region.text: the Punjab, Gandhara and the Gangetic plain

ledger.note: 225: the eastern half becomes the Eastern Kushans, based in the Punjab with its capital at Taxila (Kushan Empire page).

region.text: the whole Kushan realm at its end

ledger.note: 225: the Kushan Empire divides into two halves; the great empire is over. Successors: the Eastern Kushans (Punjab, Taxila, the Gangetic plain) and the Western Kushans (Bactria, Sogdia), whose land the Sasanians 'captured... in 225' (Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom page). Cliopatria keeps the undivided empire to 237.

wars.name: Kujula Kadphises' conquest of Kabul and Gandhara

zones.text: the Gaofu (Kabul) region, Puda (Paktiya) and Jibin (Kapisha and Gandhara)

wars.outcome: Kujula Kadphises 'invaded Anxi (Indo-Parthia), and took the Gaofu region' and 'defeated the whole of the kingdoms of Puda and Jibin'.
wars.note: No year on the page. Years are the page's bounds: the Kujula Kadphises page puts the Indo-Parthian invasion 'some time after 45 CE' and Kujula died in 85.

wars.name: Vima Takto's conquest of north-west India
wars.outcome: Vima Takto 'expanded the Kushan Empire into the northwest of South Asia' and 'installed Generals to supervise and lead it'.
wars.note: Reign c. 90-113 on the page; Cliopatria moves the whole Indo-Parthian shape into the Kushan shape in 91.

wars.name: Kushan-Han clashes on the Tarim frontier
wars.outcome: The Kushans allied with Ban Chao against the Sogdians in 84, then marched on him with 70,000 men and 'were defeated by a smaller Chinese force'; they retreated and paid tribute under Emperor He.
wars.note: The page dates the Kushan march to 86 in one place and 90 in another; the Kanishka page has Ban Chao fighting near Khotan in 90 against a Kushan army led by a viceroy named Xie, Kushans retreating under a scorched-earth policy. No border moved.

wars.name: Kanishka's northern Indian campaigns
belligerents: the kings of Saketa, Kausambi and Pataliputra

zones.text: Awadh, the Doab and western Bihar

wars.outcome: The Rabatak inscription claims he 'had submitted all India to (his) will'; Kushan rule reached at least Saketa and Sarnath; Pataliputra's conquest is told in a Chinese text of 472.
wars.note: Years are Kanishka's reign (127-c.151). The page names no war or battle.

wars.name: Sasanian conquest of the Kushan lands
wars.outcome: The Sasanians captured Sogdia, Bactria and Gandhara in 225 (Bactria 'around 230' under Ardashir I; the east in western Pakistan under Shapur I, 240-270), replaced the Western dynasty with Kushanshahs, and claimed Kushan land 'as far as Purushapura'.
wars.note: The page gives 225 for the capture, 230 for Ardashir's dominion in Bactria and 240-270 for Shapur I's advance into western Pakistan: three dates for one process.

certainty.note: Every frontier is approximate: the Bactrian, Indian and Tarim frontiers are inferred from cities, inscriptions and coin finds, not from lines. The Han frontier near Kashgar is the least certain.

notes:
Pages opened: the five of the 5-page budget (Kushan Empire, Kushano-Sasanian Kingdom, Kanishka, Kujula Kadphises, Vima Kadphises); the Western Satraps and Rudradaman pages, opened for the sibling dossier, are quoted only as second pages in notes.

One state or three: Cliopatria's three rows share Wikidata Q25979 (Kushan Empire 43-237, Eastern Kushans 238-346, Western Kushans 238-259). The pages treat them as one empire that 'split into western and eastern halves' after 225, the western half going to the Sasanians at once. This dossier ends the empire in 225; the halves have their own dossiers (eastern-kushans, western-kushans) starting 226, so the colour agent should give them the family colour with a variation rather than three unrelated hues. Cliopatria's 238 start for the halves is 13 years late, and its Kushan row covers 226-237 with the undivided empire (7,119 cells), which is exactly the union of the halves (7,070 cells).

Corrections: (1) the Tarim strip (the 893 cells of the 117 shape that are not in the 91 shape: Aksu, Kucha, Korla, Karashahr, Kashgar and the Tian Shan rim) is removed from the 117-183 shapes and Kashgar is drawn as a client kingdom by the ledger (only Kashgar is on a page); (2) the empire is drawn from c. 30, not 43, and ends in 225, not 237.

Unsettled: (a) Overlap with the Western Satraps: the Rudradaman page lists Sindhu-Sauvira (Sindh), Maru and Kukura among Rudradaman's lands in 150, while Cliopatria draws Sindh and part of Rajputana as Kushan until 270 and the Kanishka page's footnote (Dutt) names Sind, Gujarat and Rajputana as Kanishka's. The two claims are not reconciled by any page; the dossier records the Satraps as Kushan vassals for 127-150 (confidence 1) and leaves the shapes. (b) The Kidarite and Hephthalite end of the Kushan name is outside this state's life. (c) The capital for 30-90 is not on any page. (d) The Parthian war that Kanishka 'possibly fought off' is undated on the page and not recorded. (e) The Gangetic gains of 127 have no named opponent; Mathura's loss and recovery under Huvishka ('reasserting control over Mathura', c. 151) is not dated to a year.
